analysis.title: GS Crook - Connecting You to GS Thoughts from the Floor 3 Oct 2026
key_insights: GS commodities research says the global oil market was roughly balanced in September with visible stocks flat. Persian Gulf oil exports, including about 4mb/d of estimated dark exports, recovered to 23.6mb/d last week, just above the 2025 average.
GS base case is Brent at $85/bbl by year-end and $80 in 2027. Renewed escalation that damages more energy infrastructure is the upside price risk.

Hormuz LNG crossings are only 21% of pre-war levels versus 100% for oil. If ME LNG exports improve through winter, TTF near 70 EUR/MWh balances Q4 and can fall to the mid-40s EUR/MWh in Q1 under average weather.
If Persian Gulf LNG exports stagnate at 25% of normal through winter, GS estimates TTF would need to rise above 100 EUR/MWh to force LNG demand destruction outside Europe.

GS oil trading says the market is not ready to price a balanced environment despite higher Gulf flows. It sees Iran's ability to disrupt Strait flows as significant, and notes a third US carrier group and 10,000 more Marines heading to the region.

GS commodities sales says futures positioning is stretched across energy, near record highs in refined products, with roughly $20-25/bbl of risk premium in crude. Crude call skew sits at the 58th percentile of its 3-year history, which suggests buying of outright delta rather than options. GS sees vulnerability to a positioning flush, citing European diesel front cracks down $12/bbl w/w after the SPR announcement.

GS EM strategy says EM assets are stuck between rates and oil, and lower energy prices are needed for lasting local rates relief. Ahead of Brazil's October 4 election, it favors receiving the belly of the DI curve as the best risk-reward among Brazilian assets.
GS fair-value benchmarks for USD/BRL are 4.80 (fiscal premium fully compressed), 5.40 (September 2024 premium) and 5.80 (December 2024 premium) under a negative fiscal outcome.

Brazil polls point to a likely runoff that is virtually tied between Lula and Bolsonaro, and Polymarket has Bolsonaro ahead of Lula. GS EM FX trading calls it a 50/50 election with large positioning, and says Lula above 50% in the first round plus further fiscal measures would challenge long-Brazil positioning.

Rate-sensitive Brazilian equities have 2-3x rate beta to the headline index and trade at 10x (-0.9 s.d. vs 10 years). GS prefers rate-sensitive stocks and index call spreads in a market-friendly outcome.
Q3 S&P 500 earnings growth consensus is 27% y/y versus 33% last quarter. Median stock consensus is 9% versus 14% last quarter. GS US equity strategy expects both aggregate and median to beat.

GS equity strategy flags three things to watch in Q3 earnings: consumer revenues and margins under energy and rate pressure, AI capex guidance (2027 capex expected at $1.25-1.5 trillion), and hyperscaler ROIC against a 15% hurdle.

GS US equity sales describes light positioning: HF US net positioning in the 0th percentile, the GS Monetary Policy Factor at -8 (bottom of its 30-year range), and only 23% of S&P constituents above their 50-day average. It prefers owning upside convexity to chasing downside.

GS equity derivatives sales notes the NDX 12-month forward P/E is below its multi-year average after consolidating since early June. Investors question whether share prices follow positive earnings, citing JBL and MU prints this week. Upcoming datapoints are SEMICON West (10/13-15) and NVDA GTC Berlin (10/20-22).

GS portfolio strategy says long-duration bonds are still adding to portfolio risk rather than hedging, because energy-driven yield rises hit equities and keep the stock/bond correlation positive. It prefers short-dated rates receiver swaptions and bond-like equities (low vol, high dividend) tactically.

GS macro strategy says downside in rates is now a more interesting hedge, but it only protects against growth and financial-stress shocks. Relief in energy prices is the most direct path to lower yields, and further energy and yield increases remain the main risk to equities.

GS FX/rates strategy says duration looks cheap and real money is underweight, but the yield-oil correlation and rate-insensitive AI investment mean a catalyst is needed. Tighter financial conditions over the last ten days are starting to flip correlations toward bonds hedging again.

GS UK economics estimates real GDP is about 6% below its counterfactual path since the 2016 referendum, at least 4% on robustness checks. Rejoining the single market or a customs union could add 1-2% to GDP. A UK-EU summit is set for Nov 20.

GS UK desks see long-run upside for GBP and Gilts from closer EU ties, but little near-term trading edge. The autumn budget, rate differentials, and energy prices dominate. Gilt risk premium accounts for around 20-30bp of Gilt underperformance.

Trade idea from GS Asia: receive 1y1y KRW against 1y1y SOFR, beta adjusted, with entry at 4.23% KRW and 4.94% SOFR and a target of 30bp KRW outperformance. Also long 30yr KTB at 4.5-4.6%, targeting a 30bp rally.

The Korea thesis is that the 13% KRW rally since July reduces imported inflation (each 5% KRW appreciation cuts headline CPI by about 30bp). The market prices 4 more hikes and a 4% terminal rate versus the 3.5% BOK peak in 2023-24, and GS sees Korean headline CPI peaking near 3% in Q4.
Trade idea from GS Asia: pay 3y2y CNH CCS at 1.27% with a 1.46% target. GS sees a last leg of CNH appreciation over the next 3 months, with appreciation slowing once USDCNY reaches about 6.50.

Trade idea from GS Asia: pay 5y MYR NDIRS at 3.94% with a 4.20% target and a stop below 3.85%. Drivers are strong data-center-related loan growth, a BNM hike signal, record corporate issuance, and the 2027 Budget due October 9.

sector_views.rationale: Lower energy prices and lower rates would be a substantial boost to UK mid-cap and domestic shares. Budget and levy risks are the main concern.
They sold off on higher rates but are negatively correlated with Tech stocks that dominate benchmark indices.
2-3x rate beta to the headline index at 10x valuation, with asymmetric upside in a market-friendly election outcome.

earnings_insights: Q3 S&P 500 consensus EPS growth is 27% y/y (estimate) versus 33% reported last quarter. Median S&P stock consensus is 9% (estimate) versus 14% reported last quarter.
GS equity strategy expects both aggregate and median S&P 500 earnings to surpass consensus estimates in Q3.
Analysts have cut revenue estimates for consumer stocks and profit margins across most of the market. GS TMT expects numbers to meet or exceed expectations, with cautious forward consumer commentary.

Hyperscaler expectations are continued backlog growth, revenue acceleration and continued capex. The investor debate has shifted to ROIC, with GS benchmarking revenue growth needed for a 15% ROIC hurdle. Q2 calls from AMZN and MSFT showed positive ROIC momentum.
JBL and MU prints this week were cited as examples where positive results did not drive share price follow-through.

risk_factors: Renewed escalation damaging Gulf energy infrastructure could push oil sharply higher, with a tail toward $130.
A positioning flush in energy given stretched futures positioning and risk premium.
Gulf LNG exports stagnating near 25% of normal through winter, pushing TTF above 100 EUR/MWh.
Rising bond yields and tighter financial conditions weighing on equities.
Brazil fiscal reckoning after the election and a fiscally unfriendly outcome.
Hyperscaler capex and ROIC concerns, plus project delays and force majeures.
Consumer weakness from high gasoline and diesel prices, and margin pressure.
UK autumn budget and Sterling-negative rate differentials.
vol_and_positioning: Crude futures and spreads are near local highs with about $20-25/bbl of risk premium. Crude call skew is at the 58th percentile versus 3 years in the front.
Managed money positioning in refined products is close to record highs. Many macro books are effectively short oil in the tail toward $130.
European diesel front cracks fell $12/bbl w/w after the SPR announcement.
HF US net positioning is in the 0th percentile, with clients in protection mode into year-end.
Realized 3-month S&P correlation is at 1-year lows with implieds only slightly higher. GS prefers upside convexity.
Only 23% of S&P constituents are above their 50-day moving average.
Rates implied vols are higher, so equity downside, VIX upside, or European currency weakness may offer more leverage to a growth shock.
Short-dated rates receiver swaptions are favored as hedges.
geopolitical: Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz oil and LNG flows, including estimated Iranian disruption capacity.
US Administration signals possible escalation, including a third carrier group and 10,000 more Marines to the region.
Brazil general election on October 4, with a likely Lula vs Bolsonaro runoff.
UK government considering closer EU ties, including a customs union, single market or a second referendum, with a UK-EU summit on Nov 20.
Xi-Trump meeting goodwill supporting stronger CNH fixings.

tension_points.bull_case: Gulf oil exports are back above the 2025 average and the market looks roughly balanced, supporting a Brent move to $85 by year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets still price substantial risk premium, positioning is stretched, and Iran could disrupt flows, with a US escalation adding risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed escalation damaging more energy infrastructure, or a positioning flush that unwinds the risk premium.

tension_points.bull_case: A market-friendly outcome would rally the DI curve, which has overshot fundamentals.
tension_points.bear_case: A fiscally unfriendly result could trigger a knee-jerk sell-off and positioning is large.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Lula above 50% in the first round combined with further fiscal measures.

tension_points.bull_case: Valuations are cheap, real money is underweight, and tighter financial conditions are starting to flip correlations.
tension_points.bear_case: Yields stay tied to oil and growth is resilient with rate-insensitive AI investment, so bonds still add portfolio risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Resolution of the Gulf conflict that lowers oil and front-end pricing, or benign inflation prints.
